correctness.rationale: The all-n proof fixes input placement, Laplacian, column order, and signs. The reflection splitting gives two Jacobi systems with constant nonzero within-sector Krylov determinants. The cross-sector Vandermonde/resultant identity is a polynomial in edge weight and holds beyond spectral collisions. At uniform weight each nonzero symmetric Fourier eigenvalue crosses a simple antisymmetric one with nonzero rank-one derivative, giving exactly floor((n-1)/2) factors. A signed affine null vector yields the sole remaining factor and the path determinant fixes the sign. An exact-rational standalone checker verified 112 cases n=3..18, which supplement rather than substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact polynomial of the ordered single-endpoint Kalman matrix and its high-order unit-weight collapse were not stated in the directly relevant 2022 full spectral paper or the 2013 controllability analysis. The factor at the signed resistance resonance is known and is not claimed as new. Focused external and published research-index searches did not find the equivalent factorization. Reconstructing this invariant from the complete known eigensystem would require a nontrivial Vandermonde/eigenvector-product elimination; the present reflection-sector resultant proof supplies the collapsed answer. Historical priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An older unindexed article or thesis might contain the same explicit walk-matrix determinant.

The published 2022 complete eigensystem is mathematically strong enough in principle to imply the determinant after elimination; whether that derivation should be regarded as immediate prior coverage remains a human mathematical-priority question.

value.rationale: The natural algebraic controllability volume of an endpoint-actuated nearly uniform cycle has a clean exact formula for all sizes and weights. The result quantifies the increasingly high-order loss of controllability robustness as n grows at the symmetry-restoring weight, and separates signed-Laplacian degeneracy from rotational-symmetry degeneracy. Unlike a finite table or normalization check it establishes a structural sensitivity law for an infinite graph family.
